modern: From Antisthenes: It is royal to do good and to be spoken ill of.
original: From Antisthenes: It is royal to do good and to be abused.
notification: From Antisthenes: It is royal to do good and to be spoken ill of.
notification_original: From Antisthenes: It is royal to do good and to be abused.

explained.summary: A saying of Antisthenes, a follower of Socrates whose ideas fed into the Cynic and Stoic traditions: it is kingly to do good and be badly spoken of. Marcus, an emperor, takes it personally. Being misrepresented is simply part of doing the right thing in public life.
explained.today: The manager who makes a fair but unpopular call, or the parent who says no and is called mean, is in the same position. Doing right sometimes means accepting that people will grumble.
